skill.name: quality
skill.description: Code quality validation, formatting, linting, and pre-commit checks.
skill.summary: Code quality validation, formatting, linting, and pre-commit checks.
skill.author: ByronWilliamsCPA

security_audit.summary: The two static findings are false positives from Markdown backtick fences around documented shell commands in SKILL.md. The skill is prompt-only and lists fixed quality-tool commands; no prompt injection, exfiltration intent, or dynamic execution logic was found.

finding_verdicts.reason: SKILL.md line 28 opens a Markdown bash code block; the following lines document fixed uv-run quality commands. The file is prompt documentation, not Ruby backtick execution or dynamic shell interpolation.
SKILL.md line 42 closes the Markdown code block that began at line 28. It is not executable syntax and does not introduce command execution.

content.value_statement: Python projects need consistent formatting, linting, and pre-commit checks before review. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Black, Ruff, BasedPyright, and pre-commit workflows.
actual_capabilities: Lists Black and Ruff commands for formatting a Python project.
Lists Ruff commands for lint checks and automatic fixes.
Includes BasedPyright type checking for the src directory.
Includes a pre-commit command for all configured hooks.
Summarizes Python quality standards, rule categories, and relaxed test rules.
limitations: It depends on project tools such as uv, Black, Ruff, BasedPyright, and pre-commit being installed.
It does not define formatter, linter, or type checker configuration.
It does not inspect files unless the AI tool has workspace access.
It cannot guarantee fixes are correct without tests or review.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Python Pull Request
use_cases.description: Format code, run lint checks, and verify pre-commit hooks before requesting review.

use_cases.title: Check Repository Standards
use_cases.description: Confirm that project code follows documented Python quality rules and naming expectations.

use_cases.title: Run Pre-Commit Before Release
use_cases.description: Validate all configured hooks before a release branch or deployment review.

prompt_templates.title: Format the Project
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the quality skill to format this Python project. Report which formatter steps ran and whether files changed.

prompt_templates.title: Lint and Fix Issues
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the quality skill to run lint checks and apply safe automatic fixes. Summarize remaining issues for manual review.

prompt_templates.title: Validate Types and Hooks
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the quality skill to run type checking and all pre-commit hooks. Explain any failures with file-level guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Audit the Quality Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the quality skill to review the repository quality workflow. Compare formatting, linting, type checking, and pre-commit coverage.

output_examples.input: Format the project and report the result.
output: Applied the formatting workflow with Black and Ruff.
Formatting completed without remaining style issues.
Linting found import order and error message issues.
Type checking completed for source files.
Pre-commit hooks should be rerun after fixes.
The workflow uses an 88 character line length.
Ruff rules cover blind exceptions, error messages, private access, package files, debugger use, and logging formats.
Tests and scripts have more relaxed rules.

best_practices: Run formatting before linting so style changes are stable.
Review automatic fixes before committing them.
Use the same tool versions in local and continuous integration checks.
anti_patterns: Running fixes without reviewing changed files.
Ignoring type checker failures because tests pass.
Changing lint rules only to silence current errors.

faq.question: What languages does this skill focus on?
faq.answer: It focuses on Python projects that use Black, Ruff, BasedPyright, and pre-commit.

faq.question: Can it install missing tools?
faq.answer: No. The required tools must already be available in the project environment.

faq.question: Does it change source files automatically?
faq.answer: It can guide an AI tool to run formatting or safe lint fixes when the user asks.

faq.question: Can it replace code review?
faq.answer: No. It supports review by catching quality issues, but humans should still inspect changes.

faq.question: Does it include type checking?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented workflow includes BasedPyright checks for source files.

faq.question: Can it run all pre-commit hooks?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow includes a full pre-commit validation step when hooks are configured.
